mainKeyword: cordless lawn edger and trimmer combos
guideTitle: Best Cordless Lawn Edger and Trimmer Combos (2026)
metaTitle: Best Cordless Lawn Edger and Trimmer Combos
metaDescription: Six cordless lawn edger and trimmer combos and kits, from sweeper and blower bundles to a dedicated blade edger, compared on what each pairing really covers.
expertTake: The Greenworks 24V brushless trimmer and 515 CFM blower kit is the best all-round combo, and the Worx WG928 is the value pick for small yards. The VEVOR is the one to buy if you want a true blade edger instead of a string head. Anyone with long driveway edges should consider a dedicated edger rather than relying on a trimmer set on its side.
introParagraphs: A combo kit promises one battery for two jobs, but the pairing matters. A trimmer that converts to an edger plus a blower solves the clean-up after edging, while a dedicated blade edger solves the cut itself in a way a string head cannot.

The useful comparison is between what the second tool is, how big the battery is and how well the trimmer edges. This guide separates the kits that bundle a clean-up tool from the one tool that actually cuts a proper edge.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 12 in. Brushless String Trimmer and 515 CFM Blower Combo, 3.0Ah
products.description:
This kit has the best balance of the pairings here because both tools are brushless. A 12 inch trimmer with 0.065 inch dual line converts to an edger and has an adjustable height shaft, and the blower moves 515 CFM, which is more than the other blowers in this guide. A single 3.0Ah battery runs both.

Brushless motors on a small 24V platform mean longer runtime per charge and less heat. For a typical lot, the order of work is trim, edge and blow, and the 3.0Ah pack is large enough to finish that in one go. The trimmer is a light-duty tool with thin line, so it suits lawn edges and weeds rather than brush.

The 24V platform is smaller than the 40V line, so the tool range is narrower, but both tools in the kit are well matched to it. Keep the blower intake clear, replace the line before it shortens and store the battery indoors. If you want a single box that handles an average suburban yard, this is the one. A useful routine is to trim first, blow second and leave the edging for last, because the edger throws the most dirt. One 3.0Ah pack will do all three on a typical lot if you work quickly and keep the head clear.
products.bestFor: Average suburban yards that need trimming, edging and clean-up.
pros: Both tools are brushless on one 24V battery
515 CFM blower is the strongest here
Trimmer converts to an edger
3.0Ah battery is larger than most kits
cons: Thin 0.065 in. line suits light growth

products.name: Greenworks 40V 12 in. String Trimmer and 390 CFM Blower Combo, 2.0Ah
products.description:
Greenworks pairs a 12 inch auto-feed trimmer with a blower that moves 390 CFM at up to 110 mph, which is enough to lift wet leaves off concrete. The listing says the trimmer can slice through weeds up to 1 inch thick and the head carries a 3-year warranty, a specific commitment that few small trimmers offer.

What makes it useful for overgrown edges is the combination of the blower and the trimmer: after cutting back a border, the blower clears the clippings and the drive stays clean. The 40V battery is the older, widely sold platform, so spares and other tools are easy to find.

The pack is only 2.0Ah, which is small for both tools, so plan to work in two stages with a recharge, or buy a second battery. The trimmer's thin 0.065 inch line limits it to medium growth. Clean the blower intake and check the line before each session. Cruise control on the blower lets you hold the trigger at a steady speed without tiring your finger, which matters when you are clearing a long driveway. Treat the warranty claim as a good sign but read the terms, since head warranties usually exclude line wear.
products.bestFor: Edges and borders that have grown over and need cutting back.
pros: Blower moves 390 CFM at up to 110 mph
Trimmer cuts weeds up to 1 in. thick, per the maker
3-year head warranty claimed
Common 40V battery platform
cons: 2.0Ah pack is small for two tools

products.name: Worx WG928 20V 12 in. String Trimmer and 360 CFM Blower Kit
products.description:
The WG928 is a straightforward two-tool kit. A 12 inch trimmer converts to an edger by pivoting the head, and push-button Command Feed advances line on demand, so you never bump the head. A 360 CFM blower handles the clean-up.

It is a lower-powered system than the Greenworks kits, with a smaller blower and a 20V battery, so it suits small lawns and short edging jobs. The advantage is the price and the push-button feed, which makes line management the easiest of any kit here.

The Worx 20V pack is shared across a wide range of the brand's tools, so adding a hedge trimmer later needs no new battery. Pivot the head only when the motor is stopped, wipe the pivot after use and store the pack indoors. The head tilts 90 degrees, which also helps on slopes and under low shrubs where a straight shaft is awkward. If your lawn has a lot of bank, that tilt is worth more than a few extra CFM of blower.
products.bestFor: Small lawns and anyone who dislikes bumping a head.
pros: Push-button Command Feed advances line on demand
Pivot head converts to an edger
360 CFM blower for light clean-up
Battery shared across the Worx 20V range
cons: Less blower power than the Greenworks kits

products.name: Black+Decker 20V MAX LCC221 10 in. String Trimmer/Edger and Sweeper Combo
products.description:
The LCC221 is the smallest kit in the guide. A 10 inch trimmer converts to an edger, has an adjustable height handle with a soft grip and an automatic feed spool that continuously feeds line. A sweeper completes the pair.

A 10 inch swath is narrow, so it covers less ground than the 12 inch kits, but it is the easiest to steer around beds and fence lines. A sweeper is a better partner than a blower for a small paved area, because it moves debris without scattering it.

The cost of being small is power: it is a tool for lawn edges and light weeds. Wipe the head after use, check the line before each session and store the battery indoors. Adjust the handle height before you start, because a tool set too low or too high is what makes a light trimmer feel heavy. Keep the sweeper brush clear of twigs, which jam it more often than leaves do.
products.bestFor: Small yards with tight beds and paved areas.
pros: Adjustable height and soft grip
AFS feeds line without bumping
10 inch swath is easy to control
Sweeper handles small hard surfaces

products.name: Black+Decker 20V MAX String Trimmer, Edger and Sweeper Combo, Two Batteries
products.description:
This kit adds a second battery to the same idea. The trimmer converts to a wheeled edger for precise borders and an automatic line feed system supplies line as needed, and the sweeper clears debris afterwards. Two batteries and a charger are in the box.

The second battery is the key difference from the LCC221: you can trim and edge with the first and sweep with the second, or swap when the first runs low. It makes a bigger practical difference than any spec on the trimmer.

It is a light 20V system, so keep the expectations to lawn edges. Clean the head and the sweeper nozzle after use and store the batteries away from cold sheds. Charging one pack while using the other keeps the whole kit available for a full afternoon of yard work. Mark the two packs so you rotate them evenly and they age together.
products.bestFor: Small yards that need continuous work without a recharge.
pros: Two batteries in the kit
Wheeled edger mode for clean borders
Automatic line feed
Sweeper included

products.name: VEVOR 20V 8.8 in. Cordless Lawn Edger, 4000mAh, 3 Depth Settings
products.description:
A blade edger cuts a clean vertical edge into the turf, which a string head set on its side only imitates. This one has an 8.8 inch blade, three depth settings at 1, 1.25 and 1.5 inches, and a 4000 mAh battery driving it at up to 3,200 RPM.

The depth setting is the most useful feature, because it lets you match the blade to grass height, soil hardness and the line you want. A deeper setting cuts a distinct trench along a path, while the shallow setting just tidies the edge.

It is a single-purpose tool, not a combo, so it belongs here as the partner to a trimmer rather than a replacement. Use it with any of the kits above for a driveway or pavers. Clear soil from the blade after each session and keep it dry. Walk the line first and pick up stones, because a blade that hits a rock loses its edge and can kick the stone out sideways. Wear eye protection and close shoes, since an edger throws soil and grit at ankle height.
products.bestFor: Driveway and path edges that need a crisp, clean cut.
pros: 8.8 inch blade cuts a true vertical edge
Three depth settings from 1 to 1.5 in.
4000 mAh battery with up to 3,200 RPM
Single-purpose tool does one job well
cons: Blade wears on soil and stones

buyingCriteria.explanation: Kits pair a trimmer with a blower or a sweeper, and the choice changes the job. A blower moves more debris, while a sweeper is gentler on small paved areas. The Greenworks 24V includes a 515 CFM blower and the Black+Decker kits include sweepers.

A trimmer that converts to an edger turns the string head on its side, which works for light edging. A blade edger like the VEVOR cuts a clean vertical edge with depth control. If your edges are long, a blade is worth having.
The Greenworks 24V includes a 3.0Ah pack, the Greenworks 40V 2.0Ah and the Black+Decker combo two batteries. Two tools on one pack drain it fast, so size matters.
The Greenworks 24V is brushless in both tools. Brushless runs cooler and wastes less energy, which helps in a combo that drains a single battery. Other kits use brushed motors.
Command Feed on the Worx and AFS on the Black+Decker kits advance line without bumping. A bump-free head is easier on hard edges. It also wastes less line.
The Black+Decker LCC221 cuts 10 inches, the Worx and Greenworks 12 inches. A wider swath covers ground faster but is harder to steer in beds. Match it to your yard.

specDecoder.meaning: The volume of air a blower moves. Higher moves more debris at once, which means fewer passes over a pile of clippings. A blower with high CFM and low air speed clears loose material well but struggles with wet, stuck leaves.
specDecoder.watchFor: Greenworks 24V is 515 CFM, 40V is 390 and Worx is 360.

specDecoder.meaning: How fast the air leaves the nozzle. It lifts stuck debris such as wet leaves. Air speed gives the nozzle its punch, while CFM gives the stream its volume, so a good blower needs both.
An automatic feed spool that advances line without bumping. It saves tapping the head on the ground and on hard edges it spares the head from wear, although it can use line faster than a bump head.
How deep an edger blade cuts. Deeper cuts a trench. A shallow setting suits routine tidying, while the deepest setting is for re-cutting an edge that has grown over.
A motor with no carbon brushes that runs cooler.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Greenworks 24V trimmer and blower are brushless.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pairing fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how well the second tool completes the job. The Greenworks 24V blower and the VEVOR edger scored highest for their roles. We read each listing for what the second tool actually does and rated it against the clean-up a real yard needs. A pairing that adds a tool you will not use scored lower than a sparser kit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery value
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at battery size and count. The Greenworks 24V with 3.0Ah and the Black+Decker two-battery kit scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Edging quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared string-head edging with a blade. The VEVOR scored highest. A blade cuts through turf and soil rather than chopping grass, so it leaves a defined trench that a string head cannot match. We treated that as a real difference and not a feature checkbox.

howWeEvaluated.title: Convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at feed and adjustability. Push-button and automatic feeds scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered platform breadth and parts. Greenworks and Worx scored well.

cards.label: String edging
cards.text: The Worx, Greenworks and Black+Decker trimmers convert to edgers by turning the head. They suit light edging and save a tool.

cards.label: Blade edging
cards.text: The VEVOR cuts a vertical trench with a blade. It makes a crisper line but is a separate tool.

howToChoose.note: Choose string for light edging and a blade for long driveway edges.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a battery big enough for the whole run and an edger that cuts a clean line. A blade and a depth setting help.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The VEVOR edger offers a blade and three depths, and the Greenworks 24V kit supplies a 3.0Ah pack. Used together they cover long edges well.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if your yard is large. The Greenworks 24V brushless kit gives the best battery and blower.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if the yard is small. The Black+Decker LCC221 or the Worx WG928 are enough.

maintenance.why: Packed clippings strain the motor and hold moisture against the housing. Clear them with the battery removed and let the head dry before storing it.
Short line cuts a narrow swath. Fit fresh line before it reaches the guard.
Leaves block the intake and cut airflow. Clear it with the battery removed, and check the fan for cracks, since a damaged fan unbalances the motor and shortens its life.

Soil and stones dull the blade. Wipe and dry it, and look for chips or flats on the edge. A dull blade tears turf instead of slicing it, and it loads the motor, so touch it up or replace it when the cut turns ragged.
Cold lowers capacity. Keep at half charge.

faq.q: Is a trimmer-edger good enough for edging?
faq.a: For light edging, yes. For long driveway edges a blade edger like the VEVOR cuts a cleaner line.

faq.q: Do I need a blower in the kit?
faq.a: If you edge near hard surfaces, yes. A blower or sweeper clears clippings in minutes. Without one, edging debris ends up on the driveway and gets walked into the house.

faq.q: How big a battery do I need?
faq.a: For two tools on one pack, aim for 3.0Ah or more, as on the Greenworks 24V, or buy a second battery.

faq.q: Is brushless worth it in a combo?
faq.a: Yes, because a single battery drives two tools. Brushless motors waste less energy.

faq.q: Which is best for a small yard?
faq.a: The Black+Decker LCC221 or Worx WG928. Their narrower swaths are easier to steer around beds and fence posts. A smaller yard also does not need a big blower, so the lower CFM is not a handicap.

faq.q: Can the edger cut a trench?
faq.a: Yes. The VEVOR's depth settings go to 1.5 inches. Use the shallow setting for tidying and the deep one to define a new edge.
